title: mstack plugin manifest
description: One plugin fills one joint. The joint's contract (integrations/plugins/contracts.md) says what it must do; the manifest says how mstack reaches it. Discovery never installs anything.

status.description: adapter-pending: the backend exists in mstack but its contract adapter is not written yet; never selected at runtime.

transport.description: argv: run a command from a template. handoff: a host the orchestrator agent or owner starts. python: module with the contract functions. jsonrpc-stdio: any-language process answering one JSON request per line. mcp/http: a server endpoint.

command.description: argv template. Placeholders: {python} {brief} {cwd} {notify} {plugin_dir}; an argument that is exactly {mcp} expands to the host's per-run MCP arguments, and exactly {resume} to the filled `resume` arguments on a resumed turn (else nothing).

entry.description: python: module path relative to plugin_dir; jsonrpc-stdio: argv[0] relative to plugin_dir or on PATH; mcp/http: URL.

via.description: handoff only: who starts the host.

services.description: mstack services (infra/services) that must be running

credentials.description: Project credential files (.mstack/secrets/...) that must exist, or setting names whose values are such paths

tenant.description: mstack shared-service tool the project must be registered with (mstack tenant add --tool <name>)

capabilities.description: Optional contract features, e.g. agent: notify, resume, json-events, sandboxed (the host can't commit or call `mstack board`; `work` commits and reports after each turn); board: reactions; memory.long: hybrid-search.

expose.description: orchestrator: used by mstack itself. worker-mcp: offered to worker sessions as project-scoped MCP tools.

settings.description: JSON Schema for this plugin's per-project settings (validated before use).

mcp.description: worker-mcp: the stdio MCP server a worker session gets. Placeholders: {stack} {project} {python}.

hint.description: One line telling a worker when to use these tools; added to its brief.

mcp_style.description: agent only: how this host accepts per-run MCP servers. codex-config: -c mcp_servers.* via the {mcp} argv placeholder. mcp-json: an untracked .mcp.json in the worktree, enabled in its local settings. dsh-patch: a per-run overlay file in the worktree's .mstack/cache/, passed as `--patch <file>` via {mcp}. none: not supported.

resume.description: agent (argv) only: arguments that continue an earlier session, filled in at {resume}. Placeholder: {session} (the harness's own session id, read from `stream`).

stream.description: agent (argv) only: the host prints one JSON event per line (NDJSON). mstack reads the session id and the final text from it. Key lists are tried in order, so a renamed field only needs a manifest edit.

kind_keys.description: fields that name an event's kind (default ["type", "event", "kind"])

session_events.description: event kinds that carry the session id (default ["session"])

session_keys.description: fields holding the session id, dotted for nesting (default ["session_id", "sessionId", "id", "session.id"])

final_events.description: event kinds with the run's final answer (default ["final"])

error_events.description: event kinds that report an error (default ["error"])

end_events.description: events that end a turn, each a set of field values to match (default [{"type": "status", "phase": "turn_end"}]). A host with a stream counts a turn as finished only when one of these arrives, never from its exit code.

end_reason_keys.description: fields of the end event naming why the turn ended (default ["reason.kind"])

completed_reasons.description: end reasons that mean the turn completed (default ["completed"])

blocked_events.description: event kinds that report a tool's outcome (default ["tool_result"])

result_keys.description: fields of those events holding the outcome text (default ["result", "error"])

blocked_patterns.description: case-insensitive substrings of an outcome that mean the host refused the action (sandbox, no approval channel); reported to the owner as blockers

usage_keys.description: fields holding per-request token usage, summed per turn (default ["usage"])
